answer: Proof-of-stake functions as a barrier where an agent must commit capital to participate in consensus. An attacker attempting to scale fake nodes faces a ridge of prohibitive financial costs, as each identity requires a unique stake. Like a jetty diverting a high-velocity current, this economic weight stabilizes the network against disruption. Ultimately, the cost to control the system exceeds the sparrow of expected gains, rendering mass identity forgery economically irrational for malicious actors.
